hints: Focus on what it means when the table says U2 formed or W2 formed, a more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one from its halide.
Notice that V2(aq) displaces both U- and W-, while W2(aq) displaces only U- and U2(aq) displaces nothing.
Remember the strongest oxidising halogen molecule makes the weakest reducing halide ion, so flip the order to rank the ions as reducing agents.
walkthrough:
**Understand what a reaction means**

Think of this as a competition. If adding $V_2$ to $U^-$ gives $U_2$ formed, then $V_2$ has taken electrons from $U^-$ and forced it to become $U_2$.

General displacement equation:
$$X_2(aq) + 2Y^-(aq) \rightarrow 2X^-(aq) + Y_2(aq)$$
This only happens if $X_2$ is a stronger oxidising agent than $Y_2$.

**Rank the halogen molecules as oxidising agents**

Look row by row. $U_2$ causes no reaction with any ion, so it is the weakest oxidiser.

$V_2$ forms $U_2$ from $U^-$ and forms $W_2$ from $W^-$, so it oxidises both. $W_2$ forms $U_2$ from $U^-$ but does nothing to $V^-$, so it oxidises only $U^-$. That gives:
$$V_2 > W_2 > U_2 \text{ as oxidising agents}$$

**Flip the order for reducing agents**

A good oxidiser is easily reduced, so its own ion is reluctant to give up electrons. The order of reducing strength of the ions is the reverse of the oxidising strength of the molecules.

So strongest reducing ion comes from the weakest molecule:
$$U^- > W^- > V^- \text{ as reducing agents}$$

options.A: Incorrect. This puts V- ahead of W-, but V2 displaces W- to form W2, so V2 is the stronger oxidiser and V- must be the weaker reducer. V- should be last, not middle.
options.B: Correct. V2 is the strongest oxidising agent because it displaces both other halides, W2 is middle because it displaces only U-, and U2 is weakest because it displaces nothing. Reversing for reducing power gives U- strongest, then W-, then V- weakest.
options.C: Incorrect. This is almost the reverse of the truth. It makes V- the strongest reducer, but V2 is the strongest oxidiser, so V- must be the weakest reducer because it holds its electrons most tightly.
options.D: Incorrect. This makes W- stronger than U- as a reducer. But W2 displaces U- to form U2, proving W2 is the stronger oxidiser, so U- must be the stronger reducer.
